a: ab, ā (prep. + abl.) — from, away from; by (ā before consonants)
ac: atque, ac — and, and also (ac before consonants)
ad: ad (prep. + acc.) — to, toward; at, near
aere: aes, aeris (n.) — bronze, copper; bronze prow (abl. sg.)
agmine: agmen, agminis (n.) — column, army on the march, line (abl. sg.)
alta: altus, -a, -um — high; deep (f. nom./abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
arces: arx, arcis (f.) — citadel, stronghold, height (acc./nom. pl.)
auras: aura, -ae (f.) — breeze, air; pl. the air, the upper air (acc. pl.)
aut: aut (conj.) — or; aut… aut, either… or
caelestibus: caelestis, -e — heavenly; caelestēs, the gods (dat./abl. pl.)
cum: cum — (conj.) when, since, although; (prep. + abl.) with
dum: dum (conj.) — while; until (+ subj., of a goal looked forward to)
est: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3rd sg. pres.); also forms perfect passives (ūsa est)
et: et — and; also, even; et… et: both… and
ex: ex, ē (prep. + abl.) — out of, from
facto: faciō, facere, fēcī, factum — to make, form (perf. pass. part., n./m. abl./dat. sg.)
fuit: sum, esse, fuī — to be; there was (3rd sg. perf.)
gentem: gēns, gentis (f.) — race, people, nation (acc. sg.)
gentis: gēns, gentis (f.) — race, people, nation (gen. sg.)
haec: hic, haec, hoc — this; haec (n. pl.), these things, these words (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom. sg.)
hic: hīc (adv.) — here; hic, haec, hoc (pron.), this (m. nom. sg.)
hinc: hinc (adv.) — from here, hence; from this
hoc: hic, haec, hoc — this (n. nom./acc. sg.; m./n. abl. sg.)
iam: iam (adv.) — now, already; iam… iam, now… now
ille: ille, illa, illud — that; he, that man (m. nom. sg.)
illi: ille, illa, illud — that; illī, they, those (m. nom. pl.); to him/her (dat. sg.)
in: in (prep.) — + acc. into, onto, against; + abl. in, on
ingens: ingēns, ingentis — huge, enormous, mighty (nom. sg.)
iovis: Iuppiter, Iovis (m.) — Jupiter, king of the gods (gen. sg.)
ipsa: ipse, ipsa, ipsum — herself, she herself; the very (f. nom. sg.)
iuno: Iūnō, Iūnōnis (f.) — Juno, queen of the gods (nom. sg.)
labor: labor, labōris (m.) — toil, labour, task (nom. sg.)
moenia: moenia, -ium (n. pl.) — walls, city walls (nom./acc. pl.)
multa: multus, -a, -um — much, many; multa (n. pl.) as noun, many things (n. acc./nom. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
numine: nūmen, nūminis (n.) — divine will, divinity, godhead (abl. sg.)
ostia: ōstium, -ī (n.) — mouth (of a river), entrance (acc./nom. pl.)
per: per (prep. + acc.) — through, across, throughout; by
qua: quā (adv.) — where, by which way; in any way (after sī); also quī/quis, f. abl. sg.
quae: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., f. nom. sg.; f./n. nom./acc. pl.)
qui: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel. pron., m. nom. sg./pl.)
quid: quis, quid — who, what (interrog., n. nom./acc. sg.)
quis: quī, quae, quod — who (rel., dat./abl. pl., old form = quibus); also quis, who? (interrog.)
quo: quī, quae, quod — who, which, what (rel. or interrog., m./n. abl. sg.); quō (adv.), where to
quod: quī, quae, quod — which (rel., n. nom./acc. sg.); quod (conj.), because, that
quoque: quoque (adv.) — also, too (follows the word it stresses)
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
sunt: sum, esse, fuī — to be; there are; sunt mihi, I have (3rd pl. pres.)
talibus: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (abl./dat. pl.)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
tyrii: Tyrius, -a, -um — Tyrian, of Tyre in Phoenicia; Carthaginian (m. nom. pl.)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how
